cheatsheet.title: Create and analyze your first model

intro.description:
In this tutorial you model a small web shop as a data flow diagram (DFD), let SPARTA elicit and prioritize its threats, and mitigate some of them with a security solution.
Each step tells you what to do. Where possible a Click to perform link does it for you; otherwise do it by hand and choose Click when complete. Click the help icon in this heading to open the online version of this tutorial.

item.title: Open the SPARTA perspective
item.description: The SPARTA perspective arranges the Project Explorer on the left, the Threat Analysis view on the right, and the Properties view below the editor.

item.title: Create the tutorial project
item.description:
Create the sparta-tutorial modeling project. It already contains the two catalogs this tutorial uses:
- stride-per-interaction - Shostack.sparta: a threat type catalog that tells SPARTA which STRIDE threats apply to which DFD elements and interactions.
- SecurityPatternCatalog.sparta: a catalog of security solutions (for example SecurePipe) that mitigate those threats.
Click to perform, then Finish the wizard. More catalogs (such as LINDDUN for privacy) are available in the SPARTA catalogs repository on GitHub.

item.title: Create a DFD model
item.description:
Create the SPARTA model file that holds your system's data flow diagram:
1. Select the sparta-tutorial project as the parent folder.
2. Name the file webshop.sparta and choose Next.
3. Pick DFD Model as the model object and choose Finish.
You can also do this later by right-clicking a project and choosing New > Other... > Sparta Model.

item.title: Create the data flow diagram
item.description:
Open a graphical editor on the model:
1. In the Project Explorer, right-click the sparta-tutorial project and choose Create Representation.
2. Select the DataFlowDiagram representation and choose Next.
3. Select the DFD Model element inside webshop.sparta, choose Next, name the diagram Web shop DFD and choose Finish.
The diagram editor opens with the tool palette on its right-hand side.

item.title: Draw the system
item.description: Use the DFD Elements section of the palette: select a tool, then click in the diagram. Rename an element by selecting it and typing its name.

subitem.label: Draw a trust boundary with createTrustBoundary and name it 'Web shop'. Everything inside is under the web shop's control.
Inside the trust boundary, add two processes with createProcess: 'Web server' and 'Order service'.
Inside the trust boundary, add a data store with createDataStore: 'Order database'.
Outside the trust boundary, add an external entity with createExternalEntity: 'Customer'.

Connect the elements with createDataFlow (click the sender, then the recipient): Customer to Web server 'place order', Web server to Customer 'confirmation', Web server to Order service 'submit order', Order service to Order database 'store order', and Order database to Order service 'order details'.

item.title: Attach the threat catalog to the model
item.description:
SPARTA elicits threats using the catalogs attached to the model:
1. Click an empty spot of the diagram background, so that the DFD Model itself is selected.
2. In the Properties view, find the Resource property and add STRIDE-per-interaction - Shostack and the security solution catalog.
3. Save the diagram.

item.title: Analyze the model
item.description: Let SPARTA elicit the threats for the web shop and rank them by risk.

subitem.label: With the Web shop DFD as the active editor, run Load and Analyze Model. You can also use the analyze button in the Threat Analysis view, or SPARTA > Load and Analyze Model.
Review the threats. Each row shows the threat type, the affected elements, and its estimated risk. Sort by risk to see which threats to address first. The analysis updates as you change the model.

item.title: Estimate asset values (optional)
item.description:
Without estimates SPARTA uses default values. To make risk estimates reflect your system, right-click an element (for example Order database) and choose New Child > Estimate. Then, in the Properties view, set its minimum, probable and maximum loss and your confidence in that estimate. The Threat Analysis view recalculates the risk of the related threats.
Attacker profiles (contact frequency, probability of action, threat capability) can be added in the same way, in a separate SPARTA model with Attacker Model as its model object.

item.title: Mitigate threats with a security solution
item.description:
Protect the communication between the customer and the web server with a SecurePipe. It mitigates spoofing, tampering and information disclosure threats on those flows.
1. From the Security Tools section of the palette, add a solution to the diagram and set its type to SecurePipe in the Properties view.
2. A SecurePipe has four roles. Use the Assign Role tool to bind them: SP_sender to Customer, SP_recipient to Web server, SP_sendFlow to place order, and SP_receiveFlow to confirmation.
3. Save the diagram and watch the Threat Analysis view: the risk of the mitigated threats on those flows drops.
To keep the diagram readable, hide a solution with right-click Show/Hide > Hide Element; it keeps its effect.

item.title: Export the results
item.description: Share the analysis as a threat report or as a spreadsheet. These commands are also in the SPARTA menu.

subitem.label: Export a threat report (with the DFD diagram).
Export the threats to an Excel workbook (XLSX).

item.title: Next steps
item.description:
You have modeled a system, elicited and prioritized its threats, and mitigated them with a security solution.
To explore further, open one of the bundled examples via File > New > Example... > SPARTA. For example, Social Network analyzes privacy threats with LINDDUN. The documentation site has more tutorials, for example on creating your own solution catalogs and attacker models.
item.onCompletion: Congratulations, you finished the SPARTA tutorial! Reopen the welcome screen at any time via Help > Welcome.
